script.title: NASA sent a massive spacecraft to search a frozen ocean world
script.description: Beneath a thick crust of ice, Jupiter's moon Europa hides a massive liquid ocean. NASA's Europa Clipper is now on its way to investigate its potential for life.

shots.narration: Slightly smaller than our Moon, Europa shows a surface of water ice cracked by long reddish lines.
Beneath 15 to 25 kilometres of ice lies a salty ocean with twice the water of Earth.
Jupiter's gravity flexes the moon as it orbits, and that flexing keeps the ocean liquid.
Europa Clipper launched on 14 October 2024 to investigate this distant world.
This is NASA's largest planetary spacecraft, featuring solar arrays that span about 30 metres.
It arrives at Jupiter in 2030 to begin its detailed study of the moon.
The spacecraft will make 49 flybys of Europa to gather data.
Some of these passes will sweep as low as 25 kilometres above the surface.
